## Confirmatory analyses

```{r Load Data, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, out.width="55%"}
# Libraries -------------------------------------------------------------------
library(lme4);     library(lmerTest); library(car)
library(emmeans);  library(ggplot2);  library(ggpubr)
library(circular); library(MKinfer);  library(effectsize)
library(sjPlot);   library(dplyr);    library(devEMF)

# mean_cl_normal (used by several summary plots below) is surfaced by ggplot2
# but calls Hmisc::smean.cl.normal, so a missing Hmisc fails mid-plot rather
# than at load. Checked here without attaching it (Hmisc masks several dplyr
# verbs), matching the other explicit dependency checks in this script.
if (!requireNamespace("Hmisc", quietly = TRUE)) {
  stop("Package 'Hmisc' is required for mean_cl_normal in the summary plots; ",
       "install it with install.packages(\"Hmisc\").")
}

# Larger default text for every plot in this script: axis titles, tick
# labels, legend text, etc. all scale off base_size, rather than setting
# theme() individually on each plot and risking missing one. Any plot below
# that adds its own theme() call (e.g. the rotated per-participant labels
# further down, which need to stay smaller to avoid overlapping) does so on
# top of this, not instead of it.
theme_set(theme_grey(base_size = 16))

# Figures: saved as .emf (vector, pastes cleanly into Word) alongside the
# other outputs. devEMF is a pure-R implementation, so unlike MATLAB's EMF
# export this works the same on Linux as on Windows. Install once with
# install.packages("devEMF") if not already available.
figdir <- "V:/TIME/LatestMEGscripts/figures"
if (!dir.exists(figdir)) dir.create(figdir, recursive = TRUE)
save_emf <- function(plt, name, width = 7, height = 5) {
  emf(file.path(figdir, paste0(name, ".emf")), width = width, height = height)
  print(plt)
  invisible(dev.off())
}

ForCol <- "#F8766D"   # forgotten
RemCol <- "#7CAE00"   # remembered

# One seed for the whole script. Note that seeds set once at the top do not
# protect individual resampling calls further down: anything random that runs
# in between changes the state they inherit. Every bootstrap below therefore
# reseeds immediately before it runs.
SEED <- 13021996
set.seed(SEED)

# Effect coding for the factors, so that the Type III tests below (car::Anova,
# type = 3) are the intended marginal tests. Under R's default treatment
# contrasts, a Type III test of a main effect in a model that also contains an
# interaction is the effect at the OTHER term's reference level, not averaged
# over it -- misleading for the several `* Condition` models here. contr.sum
# makes those rows marginal. Note this also changes how summary() coefficients
# read (deviations from the grand mean rather than from a reference level);
# emmeans/emtrends/pairs are unaffected either way.
options(contrasts = c("contr.sum", "contr.poly"))

# Data ------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The working directory must be the folder holding this script.
DatawTheta <- read.csv("DatawTheta.csv", header = TRUE)

# Variable types. Done once here rather than repeated per chunk.
#
# The raw CSV stores this condition as "NoFlicker"; it is relabelled to
# "LongNoFlicker" immediately below for display everywhere in this script
# (plots, tables, printed output). levels = ... below matches the actual
# strings in the data so the factor assignment succeeds, and labels = ...
# then renames that level -- doing both in one factor() call rather than
# matching then separately reassigning levels() avoids a silent NA if the
# two steps ever drift out of sync.
DatawTheta$Condition     <- factor(DatawTheta$Condition,
                                   levels = c("NoFlicker", "SyncTheta",
                                              "AsyncTheta", "SyncDelta"),
                                   labels = c("LongNoFlicker", "SyncTheta",
                                              "AsyncTheta", "SyncDelta"))

# Shared colour palette for Condition, used by every plot that colours or
# fills by Condition below, so that a given condition is always the same
# colour across figures. Values match the previously-agreed figure colours
# rather than ggplot's own default hue palette (which happens to agree on
# three of the four, but substitutes green for SyncDelta rather than orange).
CONDITION_COLORS <- c(LongNoFlicker = "#F8766D",
                       SyncTheta     = "#00BFC4",
                       AsyncTheta    = "#C77CFF",
                       SyncDelta     = "#FF9913")

DatawTheta$ParticipantID <- as.factor(DatawTheta$ParticipantID)
DatawTheta$ClipID        <- as.factor(DatawTheta$ClipID)

# Scaling. as.vector() strips the attributes scale() leaves behind; without it
# the column is a 1-column matrix, which some downstream functions handle
# inconsistently.
DatawTheta$Theta4Hz    <- as.vector(scale(DatawTheta$Theta4Hz))

# Channel-space measures, present from the 2026 rerun of MainAnalysis.m onward.
CHANNEL_MEASURES <- c("WholeBrainTheta", "VisualTheta", "AuditoryTheta", "AudioVisualTheta")
hasChannel <- all(CHANNEL_MEASURES %in% names(DatawTheta))
if (hasChannel) {
  for (v in CHANNEL_MEASURES) DatawTheta[[v]] <- as.vector(scale(DatawTheta[[v]]))
} else {
  message("Channel-space theta columns not found; skipping those analyses.")
}

# Delta counterparts, present from the 2026 rerun of Analysis.m onward.
hasDelta <- "Delta1_7Hz" %in% names(DatawTheta)
if (hasDelta) {
  DatawTheta$Delta1_7Hz <- as.vector(scale(DatawTheta$Delta1_7Hz))
} else {
  message("Delta columns not found; skipping the 1.7 Hz analyses.")
}

# Weighted delta, present only if TIME_TF.m saved a channel-resolved delta band.
DELTA_WEIGHTED <- c("VisualDelta", "AuditoryDelta")
hasWeightedDelta <- all(DELTA_WEIGHTED %in% names(DatawTheta))
if (hasWeightedDelta) {
  for (v in DELTA_WEIGHTED) DatawTheta[[v]] <- as.vector(scale(DatawTheta[[v]]))
} else {
  message("Weighted delta columns not found; skipping those analyses.")
}

cat("Trials:", nrow(DatawTheta),
    "| participants:", nlevels(DatawTheta$ParticipantID),
    "| trials with a synchronicity value:", sum(!is.na(DatawTheta$Synchronicity)), "\n")
```

```{r Model reporting helpers, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Shared reporting used by the trial-level models and the circular tests below,
# defined once so every analysis reports the same quantities the same way.

# Smallest effects of interest for the equivalence tests, on each model's own
# coefficient scale. These let a null read as "evidence of absence" vs
# "inconclusive at this n" rather than a bare non-significant p.
#
# They are NOT taken from the original studies, deliberately. The published TIME
# effect (Clouter et al. 2017; Wang et al. 2018) is a synchronous-vs-asynchronous
# CONDITION contrast on memory accuracy -- a different quantity and scale from the
# continuous MEG-predictor slopes these equivalence tests actually bound (per-SD
# phase-lag, alpha and theta-power effects), and the pre-stimulus alpha analyses
# have no original benchmark at all. Mapping the condition effect onto these
# slopes would be a false lookup. So the bound is a conventional smallest effect
# of interest: Cohen's d = 0.2 (the standard fallback SESOI when no domain value
# exists; Lakens 2017), expressed on each scale. To anchor equivalence to the
# original TIME effect instead, test the Sync-minus-Async CONDITION contrast (an
# emmeans contrast on the memory model) against that effect, not these slopes.
SESOI_LOGODDS <- 0.2 * pi / sqrt(3)   # d = 0.2 on the log-odds scale (OR ~ 1.44 per SD)
SESOI_ALPHA   <- 0.2                   # d = 0.2 = 0.2 SD of pre-stimulus alpha

# Fixed-effect table for a fitted lmer/glmer: estimate (or odds ratio) with a
# Wald 95% CI [#10], the Wald p, the smallest effect detectable at 80% power
# (MDES = (z.975 + z.80) * SE, on the coefficient scale) [#3], and -- if a
# smallest-effect-of-interest is given -- an equivalence verdict from the 90% CI
# (two one-sided tests: "equivalent" if the 90% CI is inside +/- sesoi, "effect"
# if the 95% CI excludes 0, else "inconclusive") [#1]. Ends with convergence /
# singularity / dispersion diagnostics [#12].
report_model <- function(m, exponentiate = FALSE, sesoi = NULL, terms = NULL, label = "") {
  co  <- summary(m)$coefficients
  est <- co[, "Estimate"]; se <- co[, "Std. Error"]
  pp  <- co[, grep("^Pr", colnames(co))[1]]
  z95 <- qnorm(0.975); z90 <- qnorm(0.95); zpw <- qnorm(0.80)
  keep <- if (is.null(terms)) rownames(co) else intersect(terms, rownames(co))
  tf   <- if (exponentiate) exp else identity
  mdes <- (z95 + zpw) * se                       # min detectable effect, coefficient scale

  out <- data.frame(
    term     = keep,
    estimate = round(tf(est[keep]), 3),
    CI_low   = round(tf(est[keep] - z95 * se[keep]), 3),
    CI_high  = round(tf(est[keep] + z95 * se[keep]), 3),
    p        = signif(pp[keep], 3),
    MDES     = round(tf(mdes[keep]), 3),         # exp() => minimum detectable odds ratio
    row.names = NULL, check.names = FALSE)
  if (!is.null(sesoi)) {
    lo90 <- est[keep] - z90 * se[keep]; hi90 <- est[keep] + z90 * se[keep]
    lo95 <- est[keep] - z95 * se[keep]; hi95 <- est[keep] + z95 * se[keep]
    out$equivalence <- ifelse(lo90 > -sesoi & hi90 < sesoi, "equivalent",
                       ifelse(lo95 > 0 | hi95 < 0,          "effect",
                                                            "inconclusive"))
  }
  if (nzchar(label)) cat("\n---", label, "---\n")
  print(out, row.names = FALSE)
  cat(sprintf("  diagnostics: converged=%s | singular=%s | dispersion=%s\n",
              !.conv_warn(m), lme4::isSingular(m), .disp_ratio(m)))
  invisible(out)
}

.conv_warn  <- function(m) length(tryCatch(m@optinfo$conv$lme4$messages,
                                           error = function(e) NULL)) > 0
.disp_ratio <- function(m) {                     # Pearson overdispersion; ~1 good
  fam <- tryCatch(family(m)$family, error = function(e) "gaussian")
  if (!identical(fam, "binomial")) return("NA (gaussian)")
  sprintf("%.2f", sum(residuals(m, type = "pearson")^2) / df.residual(m))
}

# Bias-corrected resultant length, its uniform-null floor, and a bootstrap CI
# for a set of per-participant angles [#11]. Raw R is biased upward -- E[R]
# under uniformity is sqrt(pi/(4n)) (~0.16 at n=32) -- so a raw R near that
# floor is barely above chance. Rdbc is the same debiasing used for the MEG ITC
# weights in Analysis.m. Reseeds so the bootstrap is reproducible.
resultant_extras <- function(angles_rad, nboot = 2000, seed = 1) {
  a <- as.numeric(angles_rad); a <- a[!is.na(a)]; n <- length(a)
  Rraw  <- Mod(mean(exp(1i * a)))
  Rnull <- sqrt(pi / (4 * n))
  Rdbc  <- sqrt(max(0, (n * Rraw^2 - 1) / (n - 1)))
  set.seed(seed)
  bR <- replicate(nboot, Mod(mean(exp(1i * sample(a, n, replace = TRUE)))))
  ci <- quantile(bR, c(.025, .975), names = FALSE)
  cat(sprintf("  R = %.3f | debiased R = %.3f | null R = %.3f | bootstrap 95%% CI [%.3f, %.3f]\n",
              Rraw, Rdbc, Rnull, ci[1], ci[2]))
  invisible(c(R = Rraw, Rdbc = Rdbc, Rnull = Rnull, CIlow = ci[1], CIhigh = ci[2]))
}
```

```{r Theta power by condition, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, out.width="55%"}
set.seed(SEED)

# Helper: per-condition violin plot, used for every power measure -------------
plot_by_condition <- function(dat, yvar, ylab) {
  agg <- aggregate(dat[[yvar]] ~ ParticipantID + Condition, data = dat, FUN = mean)
  names(agg) <- c("ParticipantID", "Condition", "y")
  ggplot(agg, aes(x = Condition, y = y, fill = Condition)) +
    geom_violin(trim = FALSE) +
    geom_point(size = 2, color = "gray") +
    geom_line(aes(group = ParticipantID), color = "gray", alpha = .7) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = CONDITION_COLORS) +
    # x = NULL: the condition names on the tick labels already say
    # "condition", so a further axis title repeating that underneath them is
    # redundant. legend.position = "none": Condition is fully readable from
    # the x-axis already, so the fill legend duplicates it for no benefit.
    labs(x = NULL, y = ylab) +
    stat_summary(fun.data = mean_cl_normal, geom = "errorbar",
                 width = 0.1, color = "black") +
    stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "point", size = 2, color = "black") +
    theme(legend.position = "none")
}

# Theta power as a function of condition. Every measure uses the same
# model structure, so that they can be compared directly.
#
# Random effects: (1|ParticipantID) + (1|ClipID) is tried first for every
# measure, falling back to participant alone only if that produces a
# singular fit (lme4::isSingular -- typically ClipID's variance collapsing
# to ~0, meaning there isn't enough trials-per-clip signal to support it for
# that particular outcome).
#
# lmer, not glmer. These outcomes are continuous, and calling glmer() without a
# family argument silently falls back to a Gaussian fit, which is lmer with a
# less appropriate estimation routine and prompts a warning to that effect.

fit_with_clip_fallback <- function(outcome, data, extra_terms = "") {
  f_full <- as.formula(paste0(outcome, " ~ Condition", extra_terms,
                               " + (1 | ParticipantID) + (1 | ClipID)"))
  m_full <- lmer(f_full, data = data)
  if (isSingular(m_full)) {
    message(outcome, ": (1|ParticipantID) + (1|ClipID) was singular; ",
            "falling back to (1|ParticipantID) alone.")
    f_reduced <- as.formula(paste0(outcome, " ~ Condition", extra_terms,
                                    " + (1 | ParticipantID)"))
    return(lmer(f_reduced, data = data))
  }
  m_full
}

# Power by condition: same model structure and output for every measure, so
# they are looped over a spec list rather than written out one block each.
# The 1.7 Hz delta measures are the control for whether any effect of rhythmic
# stimulation is specific to theta, so they get the same treatment as 4 Hz
# rather than being left out; included only if present.
power_specs <- list(
  list(measure = "Theta4Hz",   data = DatawTheta, ylab = "4 Hz theta power (z)",          file = "theta4hz"))
# Visual- and auditory-weighted power get the same by-condition treatment as
# each other, with the unweighted whole-brain measure as the non-specific
# control against which any weighting-specific effect is read.
if (hasChannel) {
  power_specs <- c(power_specs, list(
    list(measure = "WholeBrainTheta", data = DatawTheta, ylab = "Whole-brain 4 Hz power (z)",        file = "wholebraintheta"),
    list(measure = "VisualTheta",     data = DatawTheta, ylab = "Visual-weighted 4 Hz power (z)",    file = "visualtheta"),
    list(measure = "AuditoryTheta",   data = DatawTheta, ylab = "Auditory-weighted 4 Hz power (z)",  file = "auditorytheta")))
}
if (hasDelta) {
  power_specs <- c(power_specs, list(
    list(measure = "Delta1_7Hz", data = DatawTheta, ylab = "Delta1_7Hz (z)", file = "delta1_7hz")))
}
if (hasWeightedDelta) {
  power_specs <- c(power_specs, list(
    list(measure = "VisualDelta",   data = DatawTheta, ylab = "Visual-weighted 1.7 Hz power (z)",   file = "visualdelta"),
    list(measure = "AuditoryDelta", data = DatawTheta, ylab = "Auditory-weighted 1.7 Hz power (z)", file = "auditorydelta")))
}

for (s in power_specs) {
  m <- fit_with_clip_fallback(s$measure, s$data)
  cat("\n===", s$measure, "===\n")
  print(Anova(m))
  print(summary(m))
  emm <- emmeans(m, "Condition")
  print(emm)
  print(pairs(emm))
  p <- plot_by_condition(s$data, s$measure, s$ylab)
  print(p)
  save_emf(p, paste0(s$file, "_by_condition"))
}

# Whether the condition effect itself differs between the two weightings. The
# separate models above cannot answer this: each trial contributes a visual and
# an auditory value, so the two are stacked and Condition * Weighting is tested
# directly, with (1|TrialUID) holding the pairing.
if (hasChannel) {
  DatawWeighting <- rbind(
    transform(DatawTheta, Power = VisualTheta,   Weighting = "Visual"),
    transform(DatawTheta, Power = AuditoryTheta, Weighting = "Auditory"))
  DatawWeighting$Weighting <- factor(DatawWeighting$Weighting,
                                     levels = c("Visual", "Auditory"))
  DatawWeighting$TrialUID  <- factor(rep(seq_len(nrow(DatawTheta)), 2))

  m_weighting <- lmer(Power ~ Condition * Weighting +
                        (1 | ParticipantID) + (1 | ClipID) + (1 | TrialUID),
                      data = DatawWeighting)
  if (isSingular(m_weighting)) {
    message("Weighting x Condition: dropping (1|ClipID) after a singular fit.")
    m_weighting <- lmer(Power ~ Condition * Weighting +
                          (1 | ParticipantID) + (1 | TrialUID),
                        data = DatawWeighting)
  }

  cat("\n=== Visual vs auditory weighting x Condition ===\n")
  print(Anova(m_weighting, type = 3))
  print(summary(m_weighting))
  emm_cond_by_w <- emmeans(m_weighting, ~ Condition | Weighting)
  print(emm_cond_by_w)
  print(pairs(emm_cond_by_w))
  print(pairs(emmeans(m_weighting, ~ Weighting | Condition)))

  p_weighting <- ggplot(DatawWeighting, aes(x = Condition, y = Power, fill = Condition)) +
    stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "bar", alpha = 0.6) +
    stat_summary(fun.data = mean_cl_normal, geom = "errorbar", width = 0.1) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = CONDITION_COLORS) +
    facet_wrap(~ Weighting) +
    labs(y = "4 Hz power (z)") +
    theme(legend.position = "none",
          axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
  print(p_weighting)
  save_emf(p_weighting, "visual_auditory_theta_by_condition")
}

# Same side-by-side view at the delta drive frequency.
if (hasWeightedDelta) {
  DatawDelta <- rbind(
    transform(DatawTheta, Power = VisualDelta,   Weighting = "Visual"),
    transform(DatawTheta, Power = AuditoryDelta, Weighting = "Auditory"))
  DatawDelta$Weighting <- factor(DatawDelta$Weighting,
                                 levels = c("Visual", "Auditory"))

  p_delta <- ggplot(DatawDelta, aes(x = Condition, y = Power, fill = Condition)) +
    stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "bar", alpha = 0.6) +
    stat_summary(fun.data = mean_cl_normal, geom = "errorbar", width = 0.1) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = CONDITION_COLORS) +
    facet_wrap(~ Weighting) +
    labs(y = "1.7 Hz power (z)") +
    theme(legend.position = "none",
          axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
  print(p_delta)
  save_emf(p_delta, "visual_auditory_delta_by_condition")
}

```

```{r Accuracy by theta power, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, out.width="55%"}
set.seed(SEED)

# Does theta power on a trial predict whether it was remembered?
#
# Each measure was previously fitted twice into the same object name, once with
# trial-order covariates and a random-slope structure and once without, so only
# the simpler model survived and the covariates never entered any reported
# result. The two are separated here: the covariate model is fitted first and
# compared with the simpler one, so the choice between them is visible.
#
# The covariates matter. EncodingPosition and BlockNumber capture position
# within the session, and both memory and theta power drift over a session, so
# omitting them leaves an obvious confound in a trial-level analysis.

fit_theta_models <- function(measure, dat) {
  f_cov  <- as.formula(paste0("Accuracy ~ ", measure, " * Condition + ",
                              "poly(EncodingPosition, 2) + poly(BlockNumber, 2) + ",
                              "(1 | ClipID) + (1 | ParticipantID)"))
  f_base <- as.formula(paste0("Accuracy ~ ", measure, " * Condition + ",
                              "(1 | ClipID) + (1 | ParticipantID)"))
  m_cov  <- glmer(f_cov,  data = dat, family = binomial)
  m_base <- glmer(f_base, data = dat, family = binomial)

  cat("\n===", measure, "===\n")
  cat("with trial-order covariates:\n"); print(Anova(m_cov, type = 3))
  cat("without:\n");                     print(Anova(m_base, type = 3))
  cat("AIC:\n");                         print(AIC(m_cov, m_base))
  print(summary(m_cov))
  print(emtrends(m_cov, list(pairwise ~ Condition), var = measure))
  # Odds ratios with CIs, minimum detectable effect, equivalence and diagnostics
  # for the covariate model [#10, #3, #1, #12].
  report_model(m_cov, exponentiate = TRUE, sesoi = SESOI_LOGODDS,
               label = paste(measure, "-> memory (odds ratios)"))
  invisible(list(cov = m_cov, base = m_base))
}

Theta4Hz.acc    <- fit_theta_models("Theta4Hz",    DatawTheta)

p_theta4hz_memmodel <- plot_model(Theta4Hz.acc$cov)
print(p_theta4hz_memmodel)
save_emf(p_theta4hz_memmodel, "theta4hz_memory_model_effects")


# --- Simple models (no covariates, no Condition interaction) ---
# A minimal specification for each measure, requested alongside the
# covariate-adjusted models above: does the measure predict accuracy at all,
# collapsing across Condition and without the trial-order covariates. Useful
# as a plain baseline against which to judge whether the covariates or the
# Condition interaction in the fuller models above are earning their keep.
fit_simple_theta_model <- function(measure, dat) {
  f_full <- as.formula(paste0("Accuracy ~ ", measure,
                               " + (1 | ParticipantID) + (1 | ClipID)"))
  m_full <- glmer(f_full, data = dat, family = binomial)
  if (isSingular(m_full)) {
    message(measure, " (simple model): (1|ParticipantID) + (1|ClipID) was ",
            "singular; falling back to (1|ParticipantID) alone.")
    f_reduced <- as.formula(paste0("Accuracy ~ ", measure, " + (1 | ParticipantID)"))
    return(glmer(f_reduced, data = dat, family = binomial))
  }
  m_full
}

Theta4Hz.simple    <- fit_simple_theta_model("Theta4Hz",    DatawTheta)

for (nm in c("Theta4Hz.simple")) {
  cat("\n===", nm, "===\n")
  print(Anova(get(nm), type = 3))
  print(summary(get(nm))$coefficients)
}

# --- No-flicker condition alone ---
# A control: with no rhythmic drive, any relationship between theta power and
# memory is endogenous rather than stimulus-driven. Condition is dropped from
# the formula here because only one level remains, which is why these are
# fitted separately rather than through the helper above.
for (measure in c("Theta4Hz")) {
  dat <- DatawTheta[DatawTheta$Condition == "LongNoFlicker", ]
  m <- glmer(as.formula(paste0("Accuracy ~ ", measure,
                               " + (1 | ClipID) + (1 | ParticipantID)")),
             data = dat, family = binomial)
  cat("\n=== no-flicker only:", measure, "===\n")
  print(Anova(m, type = 3))
  print(summary(m)$coefficients)
}

# --- Combined audiovisual weighting ---
# Condition enters as an interaction, so the question is whether the
# relationship between theta power and memory depends on the stimulation
# rather than only whether it exists on average. Same helper as Theta4Hz, so
# the two are directly comparable.
if (hasChannel) {
  AudioVisualTheta.acc <- fit_theta_models("AudioVisualTheta", DatawTheta)

  p_av_memmodel <- plot_model(AudioVisualTheta.acc$cov)
  print(p_av_memmodel)
  save_emf(p_av_memmodel, "audiovisualtheta_memory_model_effects")
}
```

```{r Phase synchrony by condition, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, out.width="55%"}
set.seed(SEED)

# Is the measured visual-auditory phase difference concentrated, and where?
#
# Per-participant circular means. mean.circular() is used rather than mean():
# an arithmetic mean of angles is wrong wherever the values straddle the
# wrap point, which they do here.
DatawPhase <- DatawTheta[DatawTheta$Condition %in% c("SyncTheta", "AsyncTheta") &
                         !is.na(DatawTheta$Synchronicity), ]

circ_mean_by <- function(dat, cond) {
  sub <- dat[dat$Condition == cond, ]
  vapply(split(sub$Synchronicity, droplevels(sub$ParticipantID)),
         function(x) as.numeric(mean.circular(circular(x, units = "radians"))),
         numeric(1))
}

SyncPhaseRads  <- circ_mean_by(DatawPhase, "SyncTheta")
AsyncPhaseRads <- circ_mean_by(DatawPhase, "AsyncTheta")

# Two questions, and they are not the same one.
#
# Doubling the angles before a Rayleigh test asks whether the values cluster
# on an AXIS, treating 0 and 180 degrees as equivalent. That is the right test
# for a quantity whose sign is arbitrary, and it is what the previous version
# ran, but it cannot distinguish a synchronous condition sitting at 0 from one
# sitting at 180, which is the distinction of interest here.
#
# The undoubled Rayleigh test asks whether the values cluster in one direction.
# The doubled version is kept for comparison.
report_phase <- function(rads, label) {
  cc <- circular(rads, units = "radians", modulo = "2pi")
  cat("\n---", label, "---\n")
  cat("n =", length(rads),
      "| circular mean =", round(as.numeric(mean.circular(cc)) * 180 / pi, 1), "deg",
      "| R =", round(as.numeric(rho.circular(cc)), 3), "\n")
  print(rayleigh.test(cc))                       # uniform against unimodal
  resultant_extras(rads)                          # bias-corrected R + bootstrap CI [#11]
  cc2 <- circular(2 * rads, units = "radians", modulo = "2pi")
  cat("axial version (angles doubled):\n")
  print(rayleigh.test(cc2))
  invisible(cc)
}


report_phase(SyncPhaseRads,  "SyncTheta")
report_phase(AsyncPhaseRads, "AsyncTheta")

# Paired difference. This is the one measure that does not depend on the
# arbitrary polarity of each participant's sensors, because a polarity error
# rotates both conditions together and cancels here. Participants are matched
# by name rather than by position, since the two vectors need not be ordered
# identically.
common   <- intersect(names(SyncPhaseRads), names(AsyncPhaseRads))
PairedD  <- as.numeric(Arg(exp(1i * (SyncPhaseRads[common] - AsyncPhaseRads[common]))))

cat("\n--- Paired Sync minus Async ---\n")
cat("n =", length(PairedD),
    "| circular mean =", round(as.numeric(mean.circular(circular(PairedD))) * 180 / pi, 1), "deg",
    "| R =", round(as.numeric(rho.circular(circular(PairedD))), 3), "\n")
print(rayleigh.test(circular(PairedD, units = "radians", modulo = "2pi")))
resultant_extras(PairedD)                          # bias-corrected R + bootstrap CI [#11]
```

```{r Accuracy by phase synchrony, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, out.width="55%"}
set.seed(SEED)

# Does the phase relationship on a trial predict whether it was remembered?

DatawSync <- DatawTheta[DatawTheta$Condition %in% c("SyncTheta", "AsyncTheta") &
                        !is.na(DatawTheta$Synchronicity), ]
DatawSync <- droplevels(DatawSync)

# Phase bin, in degrees, from the wrapped angle. Written with cut() over a
# single wrapped variable rather than as three separate which() assignments:
# the previous version used strict inequalities throughout, so a trial landing
# exactly on 45, -45, 135 or -135 degrees was silently left in the default
# "180" bin regardless of where it actually fell.
DatawSync$SyncDeg  <- as.numeric(Arg(exp(1i * DatawSync$Synchronicity))) * 180 / pi
DatawSync$SyncSort <- cut(DatawSync$SyncDeg,
                          breaks = c(-180, -135, -45, 45, 135, 180),
                          labels = c("180", "270", "0", "90", "180"),
                          include.lowest = TRUE, right = FALSE)
DatawSync$SyncSort <- factor(as.character(DatawSync$SyncSort),
                             levels = c("0", "90", "180", "270"))

cat("Trials per phase bin:\n"); print(table(DatawSync$SyncSort))

# How well does the extracted phase bin (from the recorded phase on each
# trial) agree with the condition that trial was actually run in? This is
# a trial-level manipulation check, not a test of the memory hypothesis:
# SyncTheta trials are nominally 0 deg and AsyncTheta nominally 180 deg,
# so this asks how often the phase actually measured lands in the bin its
# condition label predicts.
cat("\nExtracted phase bin by actual condition (rows = actual, columns = extracted):\n")
print(table(Actual = DatawSync$Condition, Extracted = DatawSync$SyncSort))

syncAgree  <- mean(DatawSync$SyncSort[DatawSync$Condition == "SyncTheta"]  == "0",   na.rm = TRUE)
asyncAgree <- mean(DatawSync$SyncSort[DatawSync$Condition == "AsyncTheta"] == "180", na.rm = TRUE)
overallAgree <- mean(c(DatawSync$SyncSort[DatawSync$Condition == "SyncTheta"]  == "0",
                        DatawSync$SyncSort[DatawSync$Condition == "AsyncTheta"] == "180"),
                      na.rm = TRUE)
cat("\nExtracted-bin agreement with actual condition:\n")
cat("  SyncTheta trials extracted as 0 deg:   ", round(100 * syncAgree, 1), "%\n", sep = "")
cat("  AsyncTheta trials extracted as 180 deg:", round(100 * asyncAgree, 1), "%\n", sep = "")
cat("  Overall (both conditions pooled):      ", round(100 * overallAgree, 1), "%\n", sep = "")

# Accuracy kept numeric for modelling and labelled separately for plotting.
# The previous version overwrote the numeric column with the strings
# "Remembered" and "Forgotten", which is why a second copy had to be made
# first; keeping them separate from the start avoids the order dependence.
DatawSync$Remembered <- factor(ifelse(DatawSync$Accuracy == 1,
                                      "Remembered", "Forgotten"),
                               levels = c("Forgotten", "Remembered"))

# --- Per-participant circular means by subsequent memory, and the
#     remembered-minus-forgotten angular difference tested against uniformity.
# Helper so the pooled and SyncTheta-only versions cannot drift apart.
# A participant is only included if they have both a remembered and a
# forgotten trial to take a circular mean over, so n can be < 32 (e.g. someone
# with only forgotten SyncTheta trials drops out of the SyncTheta-only version,
# though they may still contribute to the pooled one via their AsyncTheta trials).
#
# The remembered-minus-forgotten difference uses Arg(exp(i*d)), which wraps to
# (-pi, pi] correctly. (The previous version computed ((R - F) %% pi) - pi,
# which folds onto a half circle and forced every value negative: a true +10
# came out as -170.) The wide columns are renamed by the names reshape actually
# produces, not by position, so a change to the Remembered factor's level order
# cannot silently flip the sign of the difference.
phase_by_memory <- function(dat, label) {
  sdf <- do.call(rbind, lapply(
    split(dat, list(dat$ParticipantID, dat$Remembered), drop = TRUE),
    function(d) data.frame(
      ParticipantID = d$ParticipantID[1],
      Remembered    = d$Remembered[1],
      Synchronicity = as.numeric(mean.circular(circular(d$Synchronicity, units = "radians"))),
      n             = nrow(d))))

  # Widen both the per-participant mean and its trial count, so the difference
  # can be weighted by how many trials each side rests on.
  w <- reshape(sdf[, c("ParticipantID", "Remembered", "Synchronicity", "n")],
               idvar = "ParticipantID", timevar = "Remembered", direction = "wide")
  w$Forgotten  <- w[["Synchronicity.Forgotten"]]
  w$Remembered <- w[["Synchronicity.Remembered"]]
  w <- w[complete.cases(w[, c("Forgotten", "Remembered")]), ]
  w$SynchronyDiff <- as.numeric(Arg(exp(1i * (w$Remembered - w$Forgotten))))

  # Weight [#8]: harmonic mean of the two trial counts -- the effective n behind
  # each participant's difference -- so someone resting on a handful of trials
  # counts less than someone with many. (The trial-level circular GLMM would be
  # the fully principled version; this is the two-stage estimate made trial-count
  # aware.)
  w$wt <- 2 / (1 / w[["n.Forgotten"]] + 1 / w[["n.Remembered"]])
  Rw   <- Mod(sum(w$wt * exp(1i * w$SynchronyDiff)) / sum(w$wt))
  muW  <- Arg(sum(w$wt * exp(1i * w$SynchronyDiff)))

  cat(sprintf("\nRemembered minus forgotten phase angle%s:\n", label))
  cat("  n =", nrow(w),
      "| circular mean =", round(as.numeric(mean.circular(circular(w$SynchronyDiff))) * 180 / pi, 1), "deg",
      "| R =", round(as.numeric(rho.circular(circular(w$SynchronyDiff))), 3), "\n")
  cat("  trial-count weighted: mean =", round(muW * 180 / pi, 1), "deg | R =", round(Rw, 3),
      "| effective n range", paste(round(range(w$wt), 1), collapse = "-"), "\n")
  print(rayleigh.test(circular(w$SynchronyDiff, units = "radians", modulo = "2pi")))
  resultant_extras(w$SynchronyDiff)                # bias-corrected R + bootstrap CI [#11]
  list(sum_df = sdf, wide = w)
}

pooled   <- phase_by_memory(DatawSync, "")
sum_df   <- pooled$sum_df;   wide      <- pooled$wide
syncOnly <- phase_by_memory(DatawSync[DatawSync$Condition == "SyncTheta", ],
                            ", SyncTheta trials only")
sum_df_Sync <- syncOnly$sum_df; wide_Sync <- syncOnly$wide


# --- Accuracy by phase bin ---
msum_df <- aggregate(Accuracy ~ SyncSort + ParticipantID, data = DatawSync, FUN = mean)

# Bootstrap comparison of the 0 deg bin against everything else. Reseeded
# immediately before the call. The previous version compared bins labelled
# "Async" and "Sync" that were built with a different rule from the one used
# for SyncSort, then computed Cohen's d from two objects (SyncTheta_SyncDelta
# and SyncTheta_AsyncTheta) that are never defined anywhere in the script, so
# it would have stopped with an error at that point.
#
# "All other bins" is every trial not extracted into the 0 deg bin (90, 180
# and 270 deg together), aggregated once per participant directly from the
# trial-level data rather than by averaging the three bin means. This means
# a participant's "other" value is a trial-weighted mean across whichever of
# those three bins they contributed trials to, not an equal-weighted average
# of three bin means -- consistent with how every other per-participant
# accuracy figure in this script is computed.
bin0     <- msum_df[msum_df$SyncSort == "0", ]
binOther <- aggregate(Accuracy ~ ParticipantID,
                       data = DatawSync[DatawSync$SyncSort != "0", ], FUN = mean)
paired_ids <- intersect(bin0$ParticipantID, binOther$ParticipantID)
a0     <- bin0[match(paired_ids, bin0$ParticipantID),         "Accuracy"]
aOther <- binOther[match(paired_ids, binOther$ParticipantID), "Accuracy"]

set.seed(SEED)
(Bin0_vs_Other <- boot.t.test(a0, aOther,
                              alternative = "two.sided", mu = 0, paired = TRUE,
                              var.equal = FALSE, conf.level = 0.95,
                              R = 100000, symmetric = FALSE))
cohens_d(a0, aOther, paired = TRUE)

# Omnibus test across all four bins, rather than just 0 deg vs everything
# else: does accuracy differ overall as a function of which bin the trial's
# phase was extracted into? Two versions, matching the two approaches used
# elsewhere in this section:
#
# Trial-averaged: fitted on msum_df, the same per-participant, per-bin mean
# accuracy used in the comparison above. Averaging within participant within
# bin already collapses across clips, so there is no ClipID left to give a
# random intercept to, and the outcome is a continuous proportion rather than
# a binary trial outcome, hence lmer rather than glmer.
SyncSort.omnibus <- lmer(Accuracy ~ SyncSort + (1 | ParticipantID), data = msum_df)
cat("\nOmnibus test across all four phase bins (trial-averaged):\n")
print(Anova(SyncSort.omnibus, type = 3))
(SyncSort.emm <- emmeans(SyncSort.omnibus, "SyncSort"))
pairs(SyncSort.emm)

# Trial-wise: every trial kept separate, with its own binary Accuracy outcome
# and its own ClipID, rather than first averaging away that structure. This
# uses more of the data (unequal numbers of trials per bin per participant
# are handled by the model rather than by an unweighted per-participant mean
# first), at the cost of no longer being directly comparable in scale to the
# trial-averaged version above. Same singular-fit fallback used throughout
# the rest of this script.
SyncSort.omnibus.trial <- glmer(Accuracy ~ SyncSort + (1 | ParticipantID) + (1 | ClipID),
                                 data = DatawSync, family = binomial)
if (isSingular(SyncSort.omnibus.trial)) {
  message("SyncSort omnibus (trial-wise): (1|ParticipantID) + (1|ClipID) was ",
          "singular; falling back to (1|ParticipantID) alone.")
  SyncSort.omnibus.trial <- glmer(Accuracy ~ SyncSort + (1 | ParticipantID),
                                   data = DatawSync, family = binomial)
}
cat("\nOmnibus test across all four phase bins (trial-wise):\n")
print(Anova(SyncSort.omnibus.trial, type = 3))
(SyncSort.emm.trial <- emmeans(SyncSort.omnibus.trial, "SyncSort"))
pairs(SyncSort.emm.trial)

p_acc_by_bin <- ggplot(msum_df, aes(x = SyncSort, y = Accuracy, color = SyncSort)) +
  stat_summary(fun.data = mean_cl_normal, geom = "errorbar",
               width = .3, linewidth = 1.5, color = "black") +
  stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "point", size = 2.5, color = "black") +
  labs(x = "Extracted phase bin (degrees)", y = "Memory accuracy (proportion)") +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(.3, .55))
print(p_acc_by_bin)
save_emf(p_acc_by_bin, "accuracy_by_phase_bin")

# --- Distributions ---
# Separate plots for Forgotten and Remembered, rather than one overlaid
# figure, so each is fully legible on its own. Within a pair they share a
# radial scale (the higher of the two groups' peak bin counts): letting each
# auto-scale to its own maximum would make whichever group has fewer trials
# look just as "full" as the other, which is misleading. The SyncTheta-only
# pair gets its own shared max rather than reusing the pooled one, since n is
# smaller there (reusing it would clip these bars or leave the pooled plots
# with needless headroom).
#
# polar_phase_hist takes a vector of per-participant angles in radians, plots
# them in degrees on a wrapped polar axis. -180 is dropped from the tick
# breaks because theta = "x" wraps, so -180 and 180 are the same point and
# labelling both prints two overlapping ticks; 180 alone still marks it.
syncBreaks <- seq(-180, 180, length.out = 25)

polar_phase_hist <- function(vals_rad, title, fill = NULL, ymax = NULL,
                             bins = NULL, breaks = NULL,
                             inner_radius = .05, xlab = "Phase difference (degrees)") {
  g <- if (!is.null(breaks)) geom_histogram(breaks = breaks, fill = fill)
       else                  geom_histogram(bins = bins)
  p <- ggplot(data.frame(deg = vals_rad * 180 / pi), aes(x = deg)) + g +
    coord_radial(theta = "x", inner.radius = inner_radius, start = -pi/2, expand = FALSE) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(-90, 0, 90, 180), limits = c(-180, 180)) +
    labs(title = title, x = xlab)
  if (!is.null(ymax)) p <- p + ylim(0, ymax)
  p
}

# Three plots per analysis (forgotten, remembered, their difference), for the
# pooled data and again for SyncTheta only.
plot_phase_distributions <- function(sdf, wdf, suffix, file_suffix) {
  ymax <- 1.05 * max(
    hist(sdf$Synchronicity[sdf$Remembered == "Forgotten"]  * 180 / pi, breaks = syncBreaks, plot = FALSE)$counts,
    hist(sdf$Synchronicity[sdf$Remembered == "Remembered"] * 180 / pi, breaks = syncBreaks, plot = FALSE)$counts)

  pF <- polar_phase_hist(sdf$Synchronicity[sdf$Remembered == "Forgotten"],
                         paste0("Per-participant circular mean: forgotten trials", suffix),
                         fill = ForCol, ymax = ymax, breaks = syncBreaks)
  print(pF); save_emf(pF, paste0("phase_by_memory_circular_forgotten", file_suffix))

  pR <- polar_phase_hist(sdf$Synchronicity[sdf$Remembered == "Remembered"],
                         paste0("Per-participant circular mean: remembered trials", suffix),
                         fill = RemCol, ymax = ymax, breaks = syncBreaks)
  print(pR); save_emf(pR, paste0("phase_by_memory_circular_remembered", file_suffix))

  pD <- polar_phase_hist(wdf$SynchronyDiff,
                         paste0("Remembered minus forgotten phase angle", suffix),
                         bins = 24, inner_radius = .1, xlab = "Difference (degrees)")
  print(pD); save_emf(pD, paste0("remembered_minus_forgotten_phase", file_suffix))
}

plot_phase_distributions(sum_df,      wide,      "",                  "")
plot_phase_distributions(sum_df_Sync, wide_Sync, " (SyncTheta only)", "_synctheta")

# --- Trial-level models ---
# PhaseFit.main is the marginal specification: does phase-lag magnitude
# predict recall at all, pooling across Condition with no adjustment for it.
# Kept for comparison, but Condition plausibly affects both accuracy and the
# spread of abs(Synchronicity) a participant produces (Sync trials cluster
# more tightly than Async ones do), so a slope
# from this model alone risks confounding a Condition-level effect into the
# phase-lag coefficient. PhaseFit.additive controls for that: it adds
# Condition as a covariate, adjusting the phase-lag slope for whatever
# Condition contributes on its own, but still assumes a single common slope
# across conditions, i.e. no interaction. PhaseFit.abs is the same predictor
# again but lets that slope itself differ by condition (the interaction
# term), kept as a further comparison, since whether the interaction is
# warranted over the additive model is itself informative (see the AIC
# comparison below). PhaseFit.poly and PhaseFit.bin are further secondary
# specifications: the polynomial versions allow a non-monotonic
# relationship; SyncSort is the binned version.
PhaseFit.main <- glmer(Accuracy ~ abs(Synchronicity) +
                         (1 | ParticipantID) + (1 | ClipID),
                       data = DatawSync, family = binomial)
PhaseFit.additive <- glmer(Accuracy ~ abs(Synchronicity) + Condition +
                         (1 | ParticipantID) + (1 | ClipID),
                       data = DatawSync, family = binomial)
PhaseFit.abs  <- glmer(Accuracy ~ abs(Synchronicity) * Condition +
                         (1 | ParticipantID) + (1 | ClipID),
                       data = DatawSync, family = binomial)
PhaseFit.poly <- glmer(Accuracy ~ poly(abs(Synchronicity), 2) * Condition +
                         (1 | ParticipantID) + (1 | ClipID),
                       data = DatawSync, family = binomial)
PhaseFit.bin  <- glmer(Accuracy ~ SyncSort * Condition +
                         (1 | ParticipantID) + (1 | ClipID),
                       data = DatawSync, family = binomial)

Anova(PhaseFit.main);     summary(PhaseFit.main)
Anova(PhaseFit.additive); summary(PhaseFit.additive)
Anova(PhaseFit.abs);      summary(PhaseFit.abs)
Anova(PhaseFit.poly)
Anova(PhaseFit.bin)

cat("\nAIC comparison:\n")
print(AIC(PhaseFit.main, PhaseFit.additive, PhaseFit.abs, PhaseFit.poly, PhaseFit.bin))

# Odds ratios with CIs, minimum detectable effect, equivalence and diagnostics
# for the two primary phase -> memory specifications [#10, #3, #1, #12].
report_model(PhaseFit.additive, exponentiate = TRUE, sesoi = SESOI_LOGODDS,
             label = "Phase-lag magnitude -> memory, additive (odds ratios)")
report_model(PhaseFit.abs, exponentiate = TRUE, sesoi = SESOI_LOGODDS,
             label = "Phase-lag magnitude -> memory, x Condition (odds ratios)")

# Predicted-probability plot for the interaction specification (PhaseFit.abs):
# effect of phase-lag magnitude on recall, separately by Condition, holding
# the random effects at population level (plot_model's default for
# type = "pred" via ggeffects, i.e. predictions are not conditioned on any
# particular participant or clip). ggeffects predicts over the raw (signed)
# observed Synchronicity values and shows those on the x-axis, even though
# the model's actual predictor is abs(Synchronicity) -- so each curve is
# expected to be symmetric/V-shaped around 0, and the axis is labelled as
# signed Synchronicity (not |Synchronicity|) to match what is actually
# plotted, with a subtitle noting the model itself uses the absolute value.
# x-axis in degrees to match every other phase-lag figure in this chapter.
p_phasefit_abs <- plot_model(PhaseFit.abs, type = "pred",
                              terms = c("Synchronicity [all]", "Condition")) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = function(x) round(x * 180 / pi)) +
  labs(title = "Predicted recall accuracy from phase-lag magnitude, by condition",
       subtitle = "Model predictor is |Synchronicity|, hence the symmetric curves",
       x = "Synchronicity (degrees)", y = "Predicted probability of recall",
       color = "Condition") +
  scale_color_manual(values = CONDITION_COLORS) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = CONDITION_COLORS)
print(p_phasefit_abs)
save_emf(p_phasefit_abs, "accuracy_predicted_from_synchronicity_by_condition")
```

## Pre-stimulus alpha analyses

```{r Alpha load, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, out.width="55%"}
set.seed(SEED)

# Trial-level alpha, exported by AlphaAnalysis.m as AlphaTrialLevel_<ChanType>.csv.
#
# Statistical tests run here rather than in MATLAB, not for tidiness: the
# MATLAB versions fit a separate model per participant then test the
# coefficients across participants, discarding the differing precision of
# those estimates and dropping any participant with too few trials to fit.
# A mixed-effects model on trial-level data uses every trial, weights each
# participant by how much information they contribute, and lets sparse
# participants borrow strength from the rest.
#
# Columns expected:
#   ParticipantID, TrialNum, Condition (SyncTheta / AsyncTheta)
#   Synchronicity, EntrainStrength   phase measures from Analysis.m
#   Matched, Mismatched, Ambiguous   phase-bin labels
#   Alpha                            baseline-corrected pre-stimulus alpha
#   TrialOrder                       rank of the trial within the participant
#   Remembered                       1 remembered, 0 forgotten
#   ClipID                           stimulus identity, for a by-clip random
#                                    intercept alongside participant, as in
#                                    the theta/delta power models above
ChanType <- "MEGPLANAR"
Alpha <- read.csv(sprintf("AlphaTrialLevel_%s.csv", ChanType), header = TRUE)

if (!"ClipID" %in% names(Alpha)) {
  stop("AlphaTrialLevel_", ChanType, ".csv has no ClipID column. This file was ",
       "written by an older version of Alphaanalysis.m, before ClipID was added ",
       "to its behavioural-data merge; re-run Alphaanalysis.m to regenerate it, ",
       "then re-knit this file. (Casting a missing column with as.factor() silently ",
       "returns a 0-length factor rather than erroring here, which is why this is ",
       "checked explicitly rather than left to fail downstream.)")
}

Alpha$ParticipantID <- as.factor(Alpha$ParticipantID)
Alpha$ClipID         <- as.factor(Alpha$ClipID)
Alpha$Condition     <- factor(Alpha$Condition, levels = c("SyncTheta", "AsyncTheta"))

# MATLAB writes logicals as 0/1; make them logical again.
for (v in c("Matched", "Mismatched", "Ambiguous")) {
  if (v %in% names(Alpha)) Alpha[[v]] <- as.logical(Alpha[[v]])
}

# Trial order within participant, centred and scaled so that its coefficient is
# per standard deviation rather than per trial, and so that the intercept sits
# at the middle of the session rather than before the first trial.
Alpha$TrialOrderZ <- as.vector(scale(Alpha$TrialOrder))
Alpha$AlphaZ      <- as.vector(scale(Alpha$Alpha))

cat("Trials:", nrow(Alpha),
    "| participants:", nlevels(Alpha$ParticipantID),
    "| with a memory outcome:", sum(!is.na(Alpha$Remembered)), "\n")
cat("Matched:", sum(Alpha$Matched, na.rm = TRUE),
    "| mismatched:", sum(Alpha$Mismatched, na.rm = TRUE),
    "| ambiguous:", sum(Alpha$Ambiguous, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")

# Alpha is exported as entirely NA whenever Alphaanalysis.m found no
# significant cluster: there is then no principled sensor set to average it
# over, so it is left NA rather than substituted from an arbitrary set of
# channels (see "Sensor selection for the trial-level analyses" in
# Alphaanalysis.m). The three alpha models below all depend on Alpha, so
# this is checked once here and used to skip them cleanly -- with an
# explanatory message instead of a model object -- rather than letting each
# hit lme4's "0 (non-NA) cases" error individually.
alphaAvailable <- sum(!is.na(Alpha$AlphaZ)) > 10
if (!alphaAvailable) {
  message("Alpha is unusable (", sum(!is.na(Alpha$AlphaZ)), " non-NA of ", nrow(Alpha),
          " trials) -- Alphaanalysis.m found no significant cluster, so there was no ",
          "sensor set to compute it from. The alpha-by-match, alpha-by-entrainment, and ",
          "alpha-by-memory models below are skipped rather than fit on essentially no data.")
}

# Trials per participant in each phase group. A participant with very few
# trials on one side contributes an unstable estimate to any two-stage
# analysis; the mixed models below handle this by shrinkage, but it is worth
# seeing.
print(with(Alpha[Alpha$Matched | Alpha$Mismatched, ],
           table(ParticipantID, ifelse(Matched, "matched", "mismatched"))))
```

```{r Alpha by phase match, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, out.width="55%"}
set.seed(SEED)

# Wang et al.'s neural precondition: is pre-stimulus alpha higher before
# trials the stimulation failed to entrain?
#
# The MATLAB version averaged alpha within each participant and phase group,
# then ran a cluster test across participants. That test is over sensors and
# belongs in MATLAB. What belongs here is the trial-level version, which does
# not first collapse each participant to two numbers.

AlphaMM <- Alpha[Alpha$Matched | Alpha$Mismatched, ]
AlphaMM$PhaseMatch <- factor(ifelse(AlphaMM$Matched, "Matched", "Mismatched"),
                             levels = c("Matched", "Mismatched"))

# Ladder fallback used for all three alpha models below: start from the
# maximal structure (a random slope for the effect of interest, plus random
# intercepts for both participant and clip), and simplify one step at a time
# only if the current fit is singular (lme4::isSingular). fit_fn is a
# closure over the data/family/control a given model needs, so this works
# for both lmer and glmer callers without duplicating the ladder logic.
fit_with_slope_and_clip_fallback <- function(fixed_rhs, slope_term, fit_fn) {
  f_full <- as.formula(paste0(fixed_rhs, " + (1 + ", slope_term,
                               " | ParticipantID) + (1 | ClipID)"))
  m <- fit_fn(f_full)
  if (isSingular(m)) {
    message("Random-slope + clip model is singular; refitting with random ",
            "intercepts (participant + clip) only.")
    f_int_clip <- as.formula(paste0(fixed_rhs, " + (1 | ParticipantID) + (1 | ClipID)"))
    m <- fit_fn(f_int_clip)
    if (isSingular(m)) {
      message("Participant + clip intercepts model is singular; falling ",
              "back to participant alone.")
      f_reduced <- as.formula(paste0(fixed_rhs, " + (1 | ParticipantID)"))
      m <- fit_fn(f_reduced)
    }
  }
  m
}

# Random slopes for phase match, because the effect is a within-participant
# contrast and the question is whether it holds beyond participant-to-participant
# variation in its size. A random-intercept-only model would treat every trial
# as independent evidence about that contrast and understate its uncertainty.
if (alphaAvailable) {
  AlphaMatch.model <- fit_with_slope_and_clip_fallback(
    "AlphaZ ~ PhaseMatch * Condition + TrialOrderZ", "PhaseMatch",
    function(f) lmer(f, data = AlphaMM))

  Anova(AlphaMatch.model, type = 3)
  summary(AlphaMatch.model)
  (AlphaMatch.emm <- emmeans(AlphaMatch.model, ~ PhaseMatch | Condition))
  pairs(AlphaMatch.emm)
  # Effect sizes (z-alpha SDs) with CIs, minimum detectable effect, equivalence
  # and diagnostics [#10, #3, #1, #12]. Linear model, so not exponentiated.
  report_model(AlphaMatch.model, sesoi = SESOI_ALPHA,
               label = "Phase match -> pre-stimulus alpha")

  # TrialOrderZ is in the model rather than handled by splitting the session in
  # half. Alpha drifts upward with time on task, and if entrainment fidelity
  # drifts too then the two would correlate for a reason unrelated to
  # trial-by-trial state. A median split on trial order controls for that
  # coarsely, by treating the drift as a single step; a covariate uses the
  # actual ordering and costs nothing.

  # Per-participant means, for plotting only
  mm_agg <- aggregate(AlphaZ ~ ParticipantID + PhaseMatch, data = AlphaMM, FUN = mean)
  p_alpha_by_match <- ggplot(mm_agg, aes(x = PhaseMatch, y = AlphaZ)) +
    geom_violin(trim = FALSE, fill = "lightgray") +
    geom_point(size = 2, color = "gray45") +
    geom_line(aes(group = ParticipantID), color = "gray", alpha = .6) +
    stat_summary(fun.data = mean_cl_normal, geom = "errorbar", width = .1) +
    stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "point", size = 3) +
    labs(x = "Phase relationship on the trial", y = "Pre-stimulus alpha (z)")
  print(p_alpha_by_match)
  save_emf(p_alpha_by_match, "alpha_by_phase_match")
} else {
  message("Skipping the alpha-by-phase-match model: Alpha is unusable (no significant cluster).")
}
```

```{r Alpha and entrainment strength, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, out.width="55%"}
set.seed(SEED)

# The continuous version of the same question, using entrainment strength
# rather than a binary matched/mismatched split.
#
# The MATLAB version computed a Spearman correlation within each participant,
# Fisher-z transformed them and ran a one-sample t-test. That treats a
# participant with 20 usable trials as equal evidence to one with 90, and drops
# anyone below the minimum trial count entirely. The model below uses all
# trials at once.
if (alphaAvailable) {
  AlphaEntrain.model <- fit_with_slope_and_clip_fallback(
    "AlphaZ ~ scale(EntrainStrength) * Condition + TrialOrderZ", "scale(EntrainStrength)",
    function(f) lmer(f, data = Alpha))

  Anova(AlphaEntrain.model, type = 3)
  summary(AlphaEntrain.model)
  emtrends(AlphaEntrain.model, ~ Condition, var = "scale(EntrainStrength)")
  # Effect sizes with CIs, minimum detectable effect, equivalence, diagnostics
  # [#10, #3, #1, #12].
  report_model(AlphaEntrain.model, sesoi = SESOI_ALPHA,
               label = "Entrainment strength -> pre-stimulus alpha")

  # The per-participant correlations are still worth seeing, as a check that the
  # model estimate is not carried by a few participants rather than as the test.
  r_by_sub <- vapply(split(Alpha, Alpha$ParticipantID), function(d) {
    ok <- !is.na(d$Alpha) & !is.na(d$EntrainStrength)
    if (sum(ok) > 3) cor(d$Alpha[ok], d$EntrainStrength[ok], method = "spearman") else NA_real_
  }, numeric(1))

  cat("\nWithin-participant Spearman correlations, alpha against entrainment strength:\n")
  cat("  median", round(median(r_by_sub, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
      "| negative in", sum(r_by_sub < 0, na.rm = TRUE), "of", sum(!is.na(r_by_sub)), "participants\n")

  p_entrain_corr <- ggplot(data.frame(r = r_by_sub[!is.na(r_by_sub)]), aes(x = r)) +
    geom_histogram(bins = 15) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0) +
    geom_vline(aes(xintercept = median(r)), linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
    labs(x = "Within-participant Spearman r", y = "Participants",
         title = "Pre-stimulus alpha against entrainment strength")
  print(p_entrain_corr)
  save_emf(p_entrain_corr, "alpha_entrainment_corr_distribution")
} else {
  message("Skipping the alpha-by-entrainment-strength model: Alpha is unusable (no significant cluster).")
}
```

```{r Alpha and subsequent memory, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, out.width="55%"}
set.seed(SEED)

# Does pre-stimulus alpha predict whether a trial was remembered, and does
# that depend on the phase-offset condition?
#
# Replaces two MATLAB analyses. The first (2x2x2 repeated-measures ANOVA on
# accuracy, after median-splitting alpha and subsampling to equalise trial
# counts) discards a lot -- alpha's magnitude within each bin, trial
# ordering, whatever the subsampling drops -- leaving ~12 trials/cell (SE
# ~0.14). The second (per-participant logistic regression, t-tested slopes)
# fails for any participant whose trials are all-remembered or all-forgotten
# within a condition, and weights every participant equally regardless of
# trial count.
#
# The model below uses every trial, keeps alpha continuous, and carries
# trial order as a covariate rather than a split.

AlphaMem <- Alpha[!is.na(Alpha$Remembered), ]
AlphaMem$Remembered <- as.integer(AlphaMem$Remembered)

if (nrow(AlphaMem) > 0 && alphaAvailable) {

  AlphaMem.model <- fit_with_slope_and_clip_fallback(
    "Remembered ~ AlphaZ * Condition + TrialOrderZ", "AlphaZ",
    function(f) glmer(f, data = AlphaMem, family = binomial,
                       control = glmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa")))

  Anova(AlphaMem.model, type = 3)
  summary(AlphaMem.model)

  # The interaction is the effect of interest: Wang et al. report the
  # alpha-memory relationship in the synchronous condition only.
  emtrends(AlphaMem.model, list(pairwise ~ Condition), var = "AlphaZ")

  # A null here is more informative with a comparison model than without one.
  AlphaMem.null <- update(AlphaMem.model, . ~ . - AlphaZ:Condition)
  cat("\nLikelihood-ratio test for the alpha by condition interaction:\n")
  print(anova(AlphaMem.null, AlphaMem.model))

  # Odds ratios with CIs, minimum detectable effect, equivalence, diagnostics
  # [#10, #3, #1, #12].
  report_model(AlphaMem.model, exponentiate = TRUE, sesoi = SESOI_LOGODDS,
               label = "Pre-stimulus alpha -> memory (odds ratios)")

  # --- Binned version, for comparability with Wang et al. ---
  # Reported alongside the continuous model rather than instead of it, since
  # theirs is the binned form. Alpha is median split within participant and
  # condition, without the subsampling step, which changes nothing about which
  # trials are compared and avoids discarding any.
  AlphaMem$AlphaBin <- ave(AlphaMem$Alpha,
                           AlphaMem$ParticipantID, AlphaMem$Condition,
                           FUN = function(x) ifelse(x > median(x, na.rm = TRUE),
                                                    "High", "Low"))
  AlphaMem$AlphaBin <- factor(AlphaMem$AlphaBin, levels = c("Low", "High"))

  binned <- aggregate(Remembered ~ ParticipantID + Condition + AlphaBin,
                      data = AlphaMem, FUN = mean)
  print(aggregate(Remembered ~ Condition + AlphaBin, data = binned, FUN = mean))

  p_mem_by_alphabin <- ggplot(binned, aes(x = AlphaBin, y = Remembered, group = ParticipantID)) +
    geom_line(color = "gray", alpha = .6) +
    geom_point(size = 2, color = "gray45") +
    stat_summary(aes(group = 1), fun.data = mean_cl_normal,
                 geom = "errorbar", width = .1) +
    stat_summary(aes(group = 1), fun = mean, geom = "point", size = 3) +
    facet_wrap(~ Condition) +
    labs(x = "Pre-stimulus alpha", y = "Recall accuracy (proportion)")
  print(p_mem_by_alphabin)
  save_emf(p_mem_by_alphabin, "memory_by_alpha_bin")

} else if (!alphaAvailable) {
  message("Skipping the alpha-by-memory model: Alpha is unusable (no significant cluster).")
} else {
  message("No memory outcomes in the alpha table; skipping.")
}
```

```{r Alpha distributions, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, out.width="55%"}
# Inspection plots, moved here so that the figures sit with the tests they
# accompany rather than in a separate script.
if (alphaAvailable) {
  p_alpha_dist <- ggplot(Alpha, aes(x = Alpha)) +
    geom_histogram(bins = 50) +
    labs(x = "Baseline-corrected pre-stimulus alpha", y = "Trials")
  print(p_alpha_dist)
  save_emf(p_alpha_dist, "alpha_distribution")

  p_alpha_by_participant <- ggplot(Alpha, aes(x = ParticipantID, y = Alpha)) +
    geom_boxplot(outlier.size = .5) +
    labs(x = "Participant", y = "Pre-stimulus alpha") +
    # Kept smaller than the new global base size on purpose: 32 rotated
    # participant labels at size 16 would overlap. Bumped up from the
    # original size 6 so it isn't left far behind the rest of the figures,
    # but this one is still a deliberate exception, not an oversight.
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = .5, size = 9))
  print(p_alpha_by_participant)
  save_emf(p_alpha_by_participant, "alpha_by_participant_boxplot")

  p_alpha_vs_entrain <- ggplot(Alpha, aes(x = Alpha, y = EntrainStrength)) +
    geom_point(size = .6, alpha = .2) +
    geom_smooth(method = "lm") +
    facet_wrap(~ Condition) +
    labs(x = "Pre-stimulus alpha", y = "Entrainment strength")
  print(p_alpha_vs_entrain)
  save_emf(p_alpha_vs_entrain, "alpha_vs_entrainment_by_condition")
} else {
  message("Skipping the alpha distribution plots: Alpha is unusable (no significant cluster).")
}
```
